correctness.rationale: Ignore isolated zeros when listing the negative sign intervals. If their total length is less than 1−g, terminal-only negative regions exclude both Gauss nodes, which cannot both be even-multiplicity zeros of a nonzero cubic. The all-negative pattern already has excessive length. For a single interior interval, the affine factor in (x−a)(x−b)(alpha+gamma x) is nonnegative on the support, so nonpositive mean forces 1+3ab≤|a+b|, whence the half-width squared is at least (|midpoint|−1/3)^2+2/9. For the mixed pattern, write the terminal root as −t and the width of the interior negative interval as v. Under the putative shorter length, g<t≤1 and 0<v<t−g. Completing the square bounds the necessary nonnegative quantity a+b+c+3abc by −t+1/(3t)+3tv²/4<(3t²−1)(t²/4−1/3)/t<0. Reflection covers the opposite pattern. The exact zero-mean witness (x+g)^2(g−x) saturates the support bound and forces failure on the event all nodes are below g, modulo a null event. The distinct nodes form a full-dimensional simplicial hull by the Vandermonde determinant. An outside target violates a facet inequality; for each triple and orientation the remaining nodes are iid conditionally, so the support bound gives the stated union bound. Boundary membership has probability zero because the triple-root cubic mean is a nonidentically-zero polynomial of three continuous roots. For an interior target, mixing in a sufficiently small positive multiple of the sample centroid leaves another point of the hull, hence gives a representation with all weights positive. These facts imply both the stated finite bounds and the root limit.
